correctness.rationale: The exact ordered disjoint component probability yields a positive-mean normalization of the factorial cumulant. Its unique sign zero follows from monotonicity of q^{-ab}. The discrete logarithmic falling-factorial sum admits a convergent positive Laplace representation. For fixed t>0 the log mean-geometric sum has strictly positive second derivative by 2sinh(y/2)>y; this proves strict balance ordering for every allowed n and pair. Monotonicity of the discrete kernel yields global endpoints and exact simultaneous-sign example. Exhaustive rational checks n<=6 and strict-order checks n<=80 agree; they supplement rather than replace the analytic proof.

value.rationale: The sign of covariance among random-graph component-size counts quantifies dependence in the natural cluster-size spectrum. The theorem completely and sharply orders all pairwise sign thresholds at fixed total vertex mass, including unique balanced and maximally unbalanced extremes for every finite n, and proves simultaneous positive/negative ordinary covariances among distinct size pairs with the same total. These results explain a qualitative dependency change not available from the exact moment formula alone, and are structural uniform assertions rather than arbitrary numerical evaluations.
